scripts.build: npm run -w @interviewly/types build && npm run -w @interviewly/ai build && npm run -w frontend build && npm run -w backend build
scripts.//prisma:generate: Prisma Client is generated code, and nothing regenerates it on a developer machine: the root postinstall of @prisma/client finds no schema (it hoists to the workspace root), and a real postinstall here would run during the Docker deps stage, where only the manifests have been copied and the schema does not exist yet. So the one command that reads the generated types runs it first — a pulled schema change costs 1.5s instead of a type error naming a property rather than a cause.
scripts.//test:integration: The vitest files `test` excludes: they need a live Postgres and Redis, which the CI `unit` job has neither of. This ring writes for real and cleans up almost none of it, so both store URLs are resolved HERE, ahead of `--env-file-if-exists` — Node leaves an already-set variable alone, which is what takes `.env`'s `db:5432/interviewly` (the application's own database) out of the decision. Same precedence and defaults as cucumber.js, for the same reason (issues #170, #119): exported TEST_* first, then an exported DATABASE_URL/REDIS_URL (how CI points at its ephemeral services), then the localhost targets compose.dev.yaml publishes. `vitest.global-setup.mts` refuses whatever slips through. NODE_ENV=test moves the report queue to the `acceptance` BullMQ prefix, so an enqueue here cannot be consumed by a running production worker. LOG_TRANSPORT=stdout for the same reason the vitest configs force AI_ENABLED=false — a developer's `.env` with `elastic` puts a pino thread-stream in front of an Elasticsearch that is not running, and `shutdown.integration.test.ts` then hangs on `process.exit` forever rather than draining.
scripts.test:integration: INTEGRATION=1 NODE_ENV=test LOG_TRANSPORT=stdout DATABASE_URL=${TEST_DATABASE_URL:-${DATABASE_URL:-postgresql://interviewly:interviewly@localhost:5432/interviewly_test}} REDIS_URL=${TEST_REDIS_URL:-${REDIS_URL:-redis://localhost:6380/1}} node --env-file-if-exists=.env node_modules/.bin/vitest run --project worker --project node
scripts.//prepare: `|| true` is required for the production image builds: husky is a root dev dependency, so `npm ci --omit=dev` runs this script with husky already uninstalled and the install dies on `sh: husky: not found` (exit 127). HUSKY=0 does not help — npm still invokes the missing binary. There are no git hooks to install in a Docker build stage anyway.
